title: Durable journal, reconciliation and resume (RJ-01 to RJ-03)
objective: Make every state-changing step orceld dispatches recoverable without repeating a side effect. The download intent journal SG-000108 qualified becomes a shared kernel journal crate (RJ-01); every mutating dispatch records an intent before it runs and settles it after, and after a lost reply, crash or restart the provider's own reconciliation probe decides settled, abandoned or unknown, never re-dispatching (RJ-02); a reconnecting local client can read a bounded, factual summary of what finished, what is unknown and what each unknown step needs verified (RJ-03). Report task records (SG-000126) become durable across a restart through the same journal. This activation authorizes none of these by itself.

include: Activate the SG-000120 contract only. RJ-01, RJ-02 and RJ-03 each need their own exact-head qualified implementation PR; RJ-02 and RJ-03 each need a fresh-context security judge.

RJ-01, journal crate: move the SG-000108 intent journal (crates/orceld/src/live_browser.rs: JournalLine, journal_append, recovery of open intents, intents.jsonl) into crates/orcel-journal as a generic one-writer journal with states pending -> dispatched -> settled | abandoned | unknown -> reconciled; bounded line and file size; fsync on every append and a parent directory sync on Unix; a torn last line ignored with a typed warning; a second writer refused (fs4 lock, already a workspace dependency). intents.jsonl stays byte-compatible and every SG-000108 suite passes unchanged. The crate names no development browser feature and links into release builds only through providers that release builds carry.

RJ-02, journal and reconcile every mutating dispatch: fs write, edit, move and remove; git mutations; desktop actions; clipboard write; process spawn; and the SG-000126 report commit. Each records an intent bound to the approval digest before dispatch and settles it after. Reconciliation is per provider: fs and report compare the destination's existence and content hash with the approved digest; git probes ref and index state; desktop actions are marked unknown and need re-observation, never inferred from the UI; process records pid and start generation and probes the exit record. An unknown outcome is never retried: dependent steps are blocked until the user gives a new, explicit approval.

RJ-02, durable report tasks: SG-000126 task records survive an orceld restart through the journal, so task.list and task.get keep reporting them, and a report commit interrupted after approval is reconciled against the destination instead of written again.

RJ-03, resume summary: classify journal entries into completed and interrupted-unknown with input fingerprints (hashes only, never values; port of agent-native@9c277b79cb87eb27da538e572dd710986e2fa06d packages/core/src/agent/tool-call-journal.ts with its notice kept) and expose one read-only MCP tool task_resume_summary {task_id} -> {completed[], unknown[], next_verification[]}. It is local_only and listed only in the local profiles; adding it to core, the remote ceiling, is outside this grain and needs its own decision. Another session's or workspace's task is refused.
exclude: Any automatic retry or re-dispatch of a mutation whose outcome is unknown.
Any new mutation, approval class, approval reuse or approval carried in a journal entry or tool result.
Remote exposure of task_resume_summary or of any journal content (core profile, tunnel, relay, public edge).
Secret values, file contents or clipboard contents in journal entries (paths, sizes, hashes, states and outcomes only).
SG-000096 shell and process authority (it stays unarmed; RJ-02 journals process_spawn only as it exists today).
SG-000127 decisions (stop, takeover, signing, live browser in release builds).

authority_delta.activation: None. This packet authorizes implementing and proving SG-000120; it adds no capability, tool, dependency, listener or authority.
authority_delta.mcp: Proposed only (RJ-03): one local-only read-only tool, task_resume_summary; existing tools, schemas and the core membership unchanged.
authority_delta.filesystem: Proposed only: orceld writes its own journal files under its private state root; no user-visible file authority changes.
authority_delta.approval: Unchanged rules. Proposed only: an unknown outcome requires a new explicit approval before a dependent step; nothing is retried on a spent approval.
authority_delta.privileged: None. SG-000096 Full User shell remains unarmed.

decisions.question: Sequencing
decisions.decision: The founder, in the implementing session's chat on 2026-10-25 and recorded on tracking issue #455: "Founder sequencing: open SG-000120 (RJ-01 to RJ-03, durable journal and recovery) as an additional active grain alongside SG-000096 and SG-000127, with the canonical tests updated to record it." SG-000120 is activated on main f9d21e3af84f27c97fa460e236122bcf2a05377f and runs with SG-000096 and SG-000127 as the three open grains. Its authority (journal files under orceld's state root, reconciliation that only reduces duplicate effects, one local read-only tool) is disjoint from both.

decisions.question: Donor reuse
decisions.decision: RJ-01 and RJ-02 are BUILD_NEW from Orcel's own qualified SG-000108 journal; SPACE (space@09e922efd23b3c0d109ab64de7e567a901bcc61e docs/architecture.md) is adopted only as rules (unknown process-start outcome, execution-generation fencing). RJ-03 PORTs agent-native's tool-call journal classification with provenance recorded per the donor registry.

decisions.question: Remote resume summary
decisions.decision: The backlog card proposed task_resume_summary in local and core profiles. This grain keeps it local_only; exposing it to remote clients needs its own decision and review.

invariants: orceld remains the sole local authority; the journal records what orceld decided and did, it never authorizes.
A mutation whose outcome is unknown is never retried automatically.
Journal entries hold paths, sizes, hashes, states and outcomes, never secret values, file contents or clipboard contents.
One writer per journal; a second writer is refused; a torn last line is ignored with a typed warning, never guessed.
Existing MCP tool names, schemas, the core membership and the orcel-relay/1 frames are unchanged; the one new tool is local-only.
acceptance: RJ-01: crates/orcel-journal holds the journal; intents.jsonl is byte-compatible; every SG-000108 suite passes unchanged; a second writer is refused and a torn last line is ignored with a typed warning; a crash between pending and dispatch is listed by recover.

RJ-02: a fault-injection suite kills orceld at each transition for each mutating provider; after restart every interrupted step is reconciled as settled, abandoned or unknown and none is re-dispatched.
RJ-02: an fs or report mutation whose destination matches the approved digest reconciles as settled; a desktop action interrupted after dispatch is unknown and requires re-observation.
RJ-02: a dependent step after an unknown outcome is refused until a new explicit approval.
RJ-02: SG-000126 report tasks survive an orceld restart in task.list and task.get, and an approved commit interrupted before its reply is reconciled, not written twice.
RJ-03: task_resume_summary returns completed, unknown and next-verification entries after an induced crash, with hashed fingerprints only, and refuses another session's or workspace's task.
RJ-03: task_resume_summary is local_only, listed in the local profiles only, and core, the tunnel and the public edge neither list nor serve it.
Windows, macOS and Linux CI legs pass on each exact head.

review.alibaba_open_code_review: delegation mode per standing founder decision (2026-10-10) with manual review of excluded files
review.security_review: fresh-context security judge on RJ-02, RJ-03 and closeout; d1-local advisory only

successor_requirements.br_07: BR-07's independent browser postcondition verifier builds on the RJ-01 journal.
successor_requirements.remote_resume: A remote resume summary needs its own decision on the core profile and the remote threat model.

activation_note: No capability, tool, dependency or authority change in this activation packet. Separate implementation and closeout PRs must qualify their exact heads; activation CI alone proves nothing about the journal.
done_when: On Windows, macOS and Linux, every mutating dispatch is journaled and reconciled after a crash without re-dispatch, report tasks survive a restart, and a reconnecting local client can read a bounded resume summary, with the fault-injection suite and exact-head CI passing.
